title: Bayern Munich vs. Arsenal Combined XI: Gunners Narrowly Get the Edge
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott5:00 PM EDTArsenal and Bayern Munich faced off in 2025–26. / Julian Finney - UEFA/Getty ImagesBayern Munich vs. Arsenal is the headline fixture of Wednesday’s Champions League slate, and rightly so.

These are two of the best teams in Europe. Two of the favorites to go on and win the entire competition. The teams that finished first and second in last season’s group stage and could easily claim the same two spots again. As heavyweight clashes go, they don’t come much bigger than this.
Some of Europe’s best players will be on show here, even if a handful of big injuries and suspensions will rob audiences of the chance to see even more quality on show.
Considering all the players available for selection, here’s Sports Illustrated’s thoughts on a combined XI between Bayern and Arsenal.

David Raya is an elite stopper. / Maynard Manyowa/News Images/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesA foot injury has left Manuel Neuer doubtful for this game. Even if the legendary German is fit and healthy, Raya has done enough over the past few years to earn a place in nearly any combined XI you could imagine.
Neuer is given the sort of freedom that must seem alien to Raya and the rest of Arsenal’s backline. The stopper is there to save the ball and nothing more—and he’s amazing at doing exactly that.

Jurriën Timber has elevated his game under Mikel Arteta. / Maynard Manyowa/News Images/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesKonrad Laimer is one of the most underrated players around these days, but he’s in a battle with one of the world’s premier right backs in Timber here.
The Dutchman is a force to be reckoned with and will hope to build on his assist against Lille last time out in this competition.
Gabriel is an elite option. / Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesArsenal’s defense is perhaps the best on the planet, and Gabriel plays a huge part in that.

The towering Brazilian is imperious, bringing a combination of athleticism, ferocity and technical ability that few defenders can match. He’s even relished the need to elevate his game in the absence of the injured William Saliba.

Dayot Upamecano has finally realized his potential. / Oliver Kaelke/DeFodi Images/DeFodi/Getty ImagesThe arrival of Vincent Kompany, himself a legendary center back, has turned Upamecano’s career around.

Upamecano has listened to every word his illustrious mentor has offered up and has forced his way into the conversation for the best center back in the world alongside Gabriel. Whichever of these two has a better game on Wednesday is likely to come out on the winning side.

Riccardo Calafiori is flying for Arsenal. / Visionhaus/Getty ImagesThere’s a certain freedom about Calafiori’s game this season that we had not seen in his previous two years at Arsenal, and everyone involved seems to be profiting from that.

He might not be able to match up to Alphonso Davies in a running race—can anybody?—but Calafiori is now a genuine threat at both ends of the field, sweeping up at the back and contributing to goals at the other end of the field.

Joshua Kimmich does a thankless job in midfield. / Marcel Engelbrecht - firo sportphoto/Getty ImagesKimmich has been so good for so long now that his quality is often overlooked. “Yeah, he’s great, so what?”

His metronomic style of play provides the base from which Bayern can build in attack, where his star-studded teammates usually command the headlines. There are those that need to never forget to credit Kimmich for his understated importance.

Declan Rice was a target for Bayern in 2023. / Marc Atkins/Getty ImagesIn another timeline, Rice is turning out for Bayern Munich after speaking with Thomas Tuchel, now of England but formerly of Bayern, in the summer of 2023. Instead, he took his midfield dominance to Arsenal.
Rice was sensational when these two sides last met in the group stage last season, helping to inspire a 3–1 victory for the Gunners.

Aleksandar Pavlović has emerged as a genuine star. / Christina Pahnke - sampics/Corbis/Getty ImagesKompany will hope that Pavlović continues to avoid receiving the credit he deserves. The 22-year-old has quietly risen from academy gem to an undisputed superstar. He’s a tempo-setting passer who thrives in a possession-heavy setup, constantly looking for ways to get involved in the final third.
